items.title: AfD’s Far Right Win Puts New Pressure on Germany’s Leader Merz
items.summary: Antipathy to Chancellor Friedrich Merz was a reason the far right surged in a state election. Though he does not face a national election until 2029, his leadership is under increasing scrutiny.

items.title: Chinese Ship Takes Arctic Shortcut: Smart Business? Or a Political Flex?
items.summary: Melting ice is opening a trade route through the Arctic. China has begun the first regular service, part of its polar ambitions.

items.title: Israeli Allies Ban Trade With Settlements as U.K. Cites ‘Ethnic Cleansing’
items.summary: Britain, Canada and France on Tuesday announced sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank, with Britain saying Israel had “turned a blind eye” to violence against Palestinians.

items.title: Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis Edge Back to the Brink of War
items.summary: The Saudi authorities said dozens were injured in attacks by the Iran-backed militia and vowed to retaliate.

items.title: Carney Says Retaliation Against U.S. Tariffs Was Unavoidable
items.summary: In a video address, the prime minister said the United States was seeking “dependency, not a true economic partnership” from Canada.

items.title: Hungary Expels 10 Russian Diplomats, Signaling a Shift
items.summary: The housecleaning puts the new government more in line with how European allies relate to Moscow, tempering cozy ties developed under Viktor Orban’s administration.

items.title: Iceland Summons U.S. Ambassador Over Provocative Trump Map
items.summary: After voting against talks to join the European Union, Iceland is reacting forcefully to a slight against its sovereignty.

items.title: Online Posts Show Families’ Grief for Flood Victims on Tibet’s Side of China-Nepal Border
items.summary: The authorities have not released an official list of those missing in the Tibet flood, creating an information void that people have tried to fill.

items.title: Australian Social Media Users Could Get Power to Switch Off Algorithms
items.summary: Technology companies have been “running real-time, unregulated product testing on Australians” for too long, communications minister says.

items.title: Rubio Plans to Push Colombia’s New Leader to Tackle Cocaine Trade
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio — who is visiting Colombia, Ecuador and Peru this week — says he will talk to leaders about targeting drug-trafficking “terrorists,” and trade deals.

items.title: Politics News Site NOTUS Rebrands as The Washington Sun
items.summary: A trademark dispute scuttled its plans to relaunch as The Washington Star, so the site chose a different name.

items.title: TSA PreCheck Now Unlocks Access to Visit Airports Without a Plane Ticket
items.summary: At more than a dozen U.S. airports, T.S.A. PreCheck members can now apply to enter the secure area, even if they’re just going to meet someone on a flight.

items.title: Trump Media Launches MAGA-Friendly Truth Social ETFs
items.summary: The seven exchange-traded funds, like the God Bless America fund, are investing in companies aligned with President Trump’s worldview.

items.title: The Economic Fallout From a Potential Return to $100 Oil
items.summary: Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, is spiking again, reviving fears of inflation.

items.title: Bombardier Shares Down as Trump’s Trade War Targets Canadian Jet Maker
items.summary: The Montreal-based company’s share price dropped after President Trump threatened to bar it from selling in the United States.

items.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Prepares for a High-Pressure Premiere After Its Turbulent Shake-Up
items.summary: Nick Bilton, the new executive producer, has begun to put his stamp on the show. Up first: an exclusive interview with an officer who was aboard the F-15 fighter shot down over Iran.

items.title: Oil Climbs Toward $100 a Barrel Following Houthi Attacks
items.summary: Analysts said they expected the price of Brent crude, the international benchmark, to remain elevated for the rest of the year.

items.title: No Luxury Spared: New High-End Cruise Ships Set Sail
items.summary: The latest batch of yacht-like vessels sailing in Europe, the Caribbean and beyond offer personalized experiences, great food and spacious suites.

items.title: Why Stocks Are Defying Gravity and What Could Bring Them Down
items.summary: Investors are focused on strong corporate earnings and A.I., while looking past the war in Iran. But rising interest rates are an increasing risk to the rally.

items.title: OpenAI Says It Has Cracked One of Math’s ‘Millennium Problems’
items.summary: The company’s announcement is the most dramatic sign yet that artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming the field of higher mathematics.

items.title: Meta Introduces Muse, an A.I. Agent That Can Send Your Emails and Book Your Travel
items.summary: Muse, Meta’s new A.I. agent, acts as a personal digital assistant that connects to Facebook and Instagram, as well as third-party apps such as Spotify and OpenTable.

items.title: Apple Expected to Unveil a Folding iPhone at Annual Launch Event
items.summary: Fans of the company’s products widely believe it will unveil a folding smartphone at its annual launch event on Wednesday.

items.title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
items.summary: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

items.title: A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click
items.summary: An attack discovered by A.I. researchers could have compromised hundreds of millions of devices within hours, experts said.

items.title: Key App Developers Have Yet to Embrace Apple’s New Siri A.I.
items.summary: For the company’s new artificial intelligence system to take off, it will need plenty of support from the makers of popular apps on Apple’s phones.

items.title: Virtual Taekwondo Takes the Contact Out of a Combat Sport
items.summary: The contactless version of the Korean martial art is making its debut at this year’s Asian Games. Critics say it’s a glorified video game.

items.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
items.summary: Artificial intelligence was used to help develop a drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition. Its maker says the drug also seems to reduce the biological hallmarks of age.

items.title: How a Blacklisted Chinese Tech Giant Kept Buying America’s Best A.I. Chips
items.summary: Washington imposed sanctions on Inspur because of its work with the Chinese military. But the company’s subsidiary kept shipping Nvidia’s best chips to feed China’s leading A.I. firms.

items.title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
items.summary: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.
